{{Top}}
{{Youmay|the first Death Star plans|the [[Death Star II plans|second Death Star plans]]}}
{{Update|[[Jedi Dawn]], [[Star Wars: Dark Forces Consumer Electronics Show demo]]}}
[[File:Deathstar_blueprint.jpg|thumb|250px|Death Star blueprints.]]
{{Quote|If the Rebels have obtained a complete technical readout of this station it is possible, however unlikely, that they might find a weakness, and exploit it.''"<br />"''The plans you refer to will soon be back in our hands.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
The '''Death Star plans''' were the blueprints of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] that was the brainchild of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]].

==The plans==
{{Quote|noquote=1|&laquo;The Jedi must not find our designs for the Ultimate Weapon. If they find out what we are planning to build, we're doomed.&raquo;|Poggle the Lesser|<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
[[File:UltimateWeaponPlans-AOTC.png|thumb|left|250px|The plans given to [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] at the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].]]
The idea for the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] began when the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]] designed the Ultimate Weapon, using plans and concepts provided by [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]].<ref name="DS">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]] possessed the original (or a copy of the) plans, which he handed to [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]].<ref name="AOTC" />

Dooku attempted to flee the planet and go to Coruscant, but he was intercepted by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], and [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], who sought to capture him. Dooku defeated the two Knights. Yoda let Dooku escape with the plans in order to save Obi-Wan and Anakin. The future of the galaxy was strongly affected by this decision.<ref name="AOTC" />

Dooku fled to [[The Works/Legends|the Works]] of Coruscant and he delivered the schematics personally to [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="AOTC" /> Once the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] were over, Palpatine ordered the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to use the plans as the basis for the construction of the station. After the Death Star's completion, the plans became a prime target for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]], whose members hoped to find and exploit a weakness in the superweapon. In large part because of this, the Empire split up the plans and sent it to various places of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to prevent enemy hands from acquiring it.<ref name="EaW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>

==History==
===The Rebel Alliance acquires the plans===
====First encounter====
The top-secret Imperial weapons project headed by [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] was hinted at by several high officials, including Tarkin himself, but its true nature remained unknown for some time. The first vital piece of information about the Death Star was obtained during the [[Mission to Darkknell (Galactic Civil War)|mission]] to [[Darkknell/Legends|Darkknell]],<ref name="IaD">{{StoryCite|story=Interlude at Darkknell|book=Tales from the New Republic}}</ref> which took place sometime before the signing of the [[Corellian Treaty]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> during which [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] captured the Rebel Leaders [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]], [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], and [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] and sent them to the unfinished [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star I]] for execution. There [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] revealed them the name and the purpose of the battle station before executing them, but the Rebel leaders were saved by [[Galen Marek]], who sacrificed himself to allow them escape.<ref name="TFU">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> As the construction of the Death Star drew closer to completion, [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and Bail Organa knew that Rebels needed to obtain a complete technical readout of the Death Star. If their engineers could pinpoint a weakness in the battlestation, then the Rebels might be able to destroy it. The Alliance set into motion the biggest anti-Imperial offensive it had ever attempted: a complex, coordinated operation to compile a complete set of plans for the Death Star and transmit it to the [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']]. Various missions were undertaken by the Rebel Alliance with this purpose, but while some of them succeeded, others simply confirmed the Death Star's existence, name and purpose, which were in fact already known to the Leader of the Alliance.

====Events on Vergesso and Raltiir====
For the raid on Vergesso facilities [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]] secured the assistance of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] smuggling skills. Solo, originally extremely reluctant to involve himself in Rebel affairs, was forced to comply after Antilles made assisting him the condition for rescuing him from Imperial custody over the surface of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]].

Solo undertook a mission to infiltrate the Imperial shipping facilities in the [[Vergesso Asteroids/Legends|Vergesso Asteroids]], planting a tracking device and [[Electromagnetic pulse/Legends|EMP]] emitter in a cargo container bound for an Imperial research station in [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]]. The EMP successfully disabled the station's defenses long enough for Rebel search teams to raid the station. The data they acquired "confirmed" the existence of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star I]] and gave the Rebels an idea of the scale of its destructive capabilities, but failed to provide any technical information with which a weakness could be identified. Even [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]], Tarkin's personal slave rescued during the raid, knew little about the plot.

[[File:DSPlanChip-DF.png|thumb|250px|The plan data kept in the [[Trid]] facility.]]
Using funds stolen from the raid on [[Ylesia/Legends|Ylesia]] and other sources, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] planted and aided spies on the world of [[Ralltiir/Legends|Ralltiir]]. One of their number, [[Basso]], also "confirmed" the existence of a massive Imperial construction, code-named Death Star. This was later identified as a massive superlaser-wielding battlestation by the Empire's [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Tion (Lord)/Legends|Tion]]. Shortly before his death, Tion revealed that a convoy containing the Death Star plans was en route to [[Toprawa/Legends|Toprawa]] from Tarkin's headquarters on [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]].

====Death Star uprising====
{{Main|Death Star Uprising}}
{{Quote|After the embarrassment of the prison break, Lord Vader removed us from our comfortable billet, and began dragging the 501st across the galaxy, in a dangerous hunt for the now missing Death Star plans.|[[Retired clone trooper]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>}}
A section of the plans were stolen from the Empire during a Rebel jail break inside the nearly completed Death Star. [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]] of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], who had been guarding the plans onboard the Death Star, crushed the uprising and were thought to have recovered the plans. However, some prisoners had managed to transmit one copy to rebel forces on [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]].

====Discoveries at Orron III and AX-235====
{{Main|Battle of Orron III}}
[[File:AX-235_2.jpg|thumb|200px|left|Rebel spies on AX-235 while intercepting the schematics.]]
A [[BFF-1 bulk freighter/Legends|BFF-1 bulk freighter]] called [[Phoenix (BFF-1 bulk freighter)|''Phoenix'']] stole several [[communications satellite]]s from the Imperial base on [[Orron III]]. The freighter was later recovered by the alliance and the satellites were spread by the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[Jeffrey]]'' in the [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]] to intercept Imperial transmissions in the hopes of learning more.

Technical information from the Death Star came to the attention of outpost [[AX-235]] in the Cron Drift. Due to the importance of what had been discovered, [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]] was sent to personally courier the schematics out of AX-235, taking them to the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']]. From there, shuttle [[Maria (MC80 Star Cruiser)|''Maria'']] transferred them to [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']].

====Keyan Farlander's success====
[[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]] and members of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] protected the ''Tantive IV'' while the technical data from the [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']] [[Death Star plans delivery|transferred]] from the shuttle [[Maria (Lambda-class)|''Maria'']]. Four other corvettes were used as decoys in order to protect the ''Tantive''{{'s}} identity, but the Star Destroyer ''[[Immortal/Legends|Immortal]]'' arrived, and launched an attack on the ''Tantive''. Thanks to Keyan Farlander, the ''Tantive'' managed to escape to Toprawa.

====Mission to Danuta====
[[File:MissionToDanuta-DFRemaster.jpg|thumb|250px|Katarn in [[Trid]] witnesses a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of the battlestation on a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]].]]
{{Main|Mission to Danuta}}
Rebels on [[Danuta]] had learned that Lemelisk had visited the local research facility, and obtained video of a set of Death Star plans being held there. Rebel Intelligence hoped that the Danuta plans included additional engineering schematics and a complete map to the offensive and defensive weapons emplacements.<ref name="SFTE">''[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire]]''</ref> Additionally, the Alliance already held the intercepted technical data from AX-235 with the plans from the actual Death Star. All of this information was needed to ensure success. The Rebels on Toprawa had a shot at the convoy, while Mon Mothma recruited an Imperial defector named [[Kyle Katarn]] and the mercenary [[Rianna Saren]] to infiltrate an Imperial outpost on Danuta.

Kyle was to steal a memory matrix there that contained the plans for the Death Star while Rianna was charged with retrieving more Intel from [[Zarien Kheev]]. With the aid of [[Jan Ors]] and [[Meck Odom]], Katarn escaped the facility and transmitted this set of the plans to Rebel spies in the Toprawa system, where it was eventually passed to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Princess Leia]] on the Tantive IV. As for Rianna, she and [[Z-58-0]] also completed their objective and transmitted the plans to Princess Leia in the [[Toprawa system/Legends|Toprawa system]].<ref name="DS" />

====Battle of Toprawa====
{{Main|Battle of Toprawa}}
[[File:Leia_Organa_by_Monte_Moore.jpg|left|thumb|250px|Leia Organa observes the hologram of the battlestation.]]
Rebel Intelligence knew that the plans for the battle station's hull design and [[Life support/Legends|life support]] infrastructure were held within the Imperial Research Facility on Toprawa.<ref name="SFTE" /> The Toprawan Rebels were ordered to cripple the Imperial convoy heading for Toprawa, and steal the plans, which included a list of its potential flaws. Combined with the superlaser control system plans and other technical schematics, the Rebellion would then have a complete technical readout of the battlestation. [[Bria Tharen]] and [[Red Hand Squadron]] volunteered to accompany an Alliance infiltration team to Toprawa aboard the [[Retribution (Marauder-class)|''Retribution'']], to aid in the transmission of the plans, an operation dubbed "Skyhook", though they were unaware of the exact nature of the weapon.

The Toprawan Rebels attacked and crippled the Imperial convoy and captured the plans - an event often considered the first major victory for the Alliance. In response, the Empire blockaded the planet. Bail Organa was to have taken the [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']] to intercept the transmission of the stolen Death Star plans, but his daughter, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], volunteered to go in his stead.

====Raid on the Imperial Research Station====
The Rebels on Toprawa were without the proper equipment to transmit the plans to the ''Tantive''. They decided to attack the IRS, and use its comm station. A young man named [[Havet Storm]] was recruited to steal the superlaser control plans.

The combined Rebel forces hit the main reception building. They managed to take the communications center station, where Havet Storm arrived with the superlaser plans. Here they were ambushed by head of security Commander [[Facet Anamor|Diamond]] and her stormtroopers. While Red Hand Squadron held off Imperial forces outside the Center, Havet transmitted the plans in a quick burst, using frequency 1215. The transmission was barely in time—Imperial fire chopped the comm/sensor tower in half just seconds after the ''Tantive'' sent out a "transmission complete" acknowledgment.

====Detour to Kalakar Six====
[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], who had sworn to recapture the plans after the Death Star uprising, briefly followed up on a tip that led him to [[Kalakar Six]]. It proved to be a ruse generated by the [[Prophets of the Dark Side]], who had predicted that the Death Star would soon be destroyed. Instead, Vader chose to pursue Leia Organa to the Toprawa system, while the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] traced the Rebels from the Death Star uprising to Polis Massa.

====The Battle of Polis Massa====
{{Main|Raid on Polis Massa}}
{{Quote|We were supposed to go in, wipe out a small band of Rebels, and recover some stolen Imperial plans on an encrypted holodisk.|Retired clone trooper|<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II" />}}
The 501st Legion was sent to retrieve the plans that had been transmitted to Polis Massa. Once there, the 501st was caught up in a firefight with the Rebellion. By the time the 501st got to the plans, a copy had already been beamed from Polis Massa to the ''Tantive IV''. The [[Analysis Bureau (Imperial Intelligence)#Signal|Signal]] branch of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence's]] [[Analysis Bureau (Imperial Intelligence)|Analysis Bureau]] discovered that the plans had been sent to the ''Tantive IV'' by analyzing the unshielded ELEL (Extremely Low Energy Level) transmission from droid [[U-3PO/Legends|U-3PO]] aboard the ship. This allowed Vader to track the ''Tantive IV'' to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

====Moff Kalast and the Bothan Spynet====
Sometime prior to the Death Star plans arriving on Polis Massa, rogue Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kalast]] aided the Rebellion with information linked to the battlestation. The [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]] had acquired secret top priority Imperial codes from the Death Star and transferred them to Kalast who, in turn, delivered them to the Rebellion.<ref name="EaW" />

After learning of the combined treachery of both the Spynet and Kalast, Emperor Palpatine personally traveled to [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]] to punish the Bothans. The Emperor, along with two of his [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guards]], [[Mission to Bothawui|slaughtered]] a large number of Bothans. One Bothan, begging for his life, informed the Emperor that the plans were to be beamed to the ''Tantive IV'' in the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]]. The Emperor regrouped with Vader, who had learned the same, and ordered his servant to Tatooine.<ref name="EaW" />

===R2-D2's mission===
{{Quote|The Death Star plans are not in the main computer.|Stormtrooper to Darth Vader|audio=NotInMainComputer.flac|<ref name="Episode 4" />}}
[[File:OrganaDeathStarPlansR2D2-SWTCGCoreSet.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Princess Leia loads the plans into R2-D2 aboard the ''Tantive IV'' over Tatooine.]]
Having received the various sets of blueprints, the Rebels on ''Tantive IV'' were able to recreate a full tactical readout of the Death Star. They attempted to deliver this readout to the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Star Cruiser]] [[Liberty/Legends|''Liberty'']], but a sudden appearance of the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] ''Devastator'' caused the transfer to stop; ''Tantive IV'' moved to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to reach [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] so that he could bring it to Bail Organa on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]. Before they could succeed, though, Darth Vader led a [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|strike against the ship]] by the 501st Legion. Princess Leia, knowing the Rebels had no hope of defeating Vader's forces, placed the plans within the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], programmed him to deliver them with a message to Obi-Wan Kenobi on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and then, after being captured by Vader, denied that ''Tantive IV'' had ever received such plans.

R2-D2 boarded an escape pod with [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and journeyed through the sands of Tatooine to fulfill his mission. The plans were nearly in danger of being lost forever when [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] ambushed and enslaved R2, but a string of events led R2 to the ownership of [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]]. R2 convinced Lars's nephew [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to remove the droid's [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolt]], suggesting that doing so was the only way R2 could access the rest of Princess Leia's message (which Luke had accidentally discovered), but it was not long after Luke had done so that R2 had taken the opportunity to escape, seeking out General Kenobi. Luke and C-3PO chased R2 down, after which they stumbled across a group of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]]. Again the plans were nearly doomed, but the Sand People scattered at the arrival of one they knew and feared: Obi-Wan Kenobi. R2-D2 had completed his task.

====The trail to Yavin====
{{Quote|An analysis of the plans provided by Princess Leia has demonstrated a weakness in the battlestation.|Jan Dodonna|<ref name="Episode 4" />}}
Leia's message conveyed to Obi-Wan the urgency of bringing R2 to Bail Organa. Joined by Luke and C-3PO, they hired the mercenary [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] to smuggle them to Alderaan on the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], and they escaped from [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] spaceport in a fierce firefight.

The plans, however, would never make it to Alderaan. In a demonstration of the Death Star's capabilities, Grand Moff Tarkin had [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|ordered the planet destroyed]], and the crew of the ''Falcon'' exited [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] only to find their destination missing, while a lone [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] fled the scene. Han determined to destroy the fighter so that their location could not be reported, but following the fighter led the ''Falcon'' to the Death Star itself.

[[File:DeathStar_plans.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] briefs rebel pilots on the Death Star plans.]]
R2 was as close to the Imperials as he could be, and at one point he and C-3PO were even forced to interact with a squad of stormtroopers. Still, none of the soldiers realized that the little droid the Empire had been searching for was on the very station it posed so dangerous a threat to. When the crew of the ''Falcon'' escaped with Princess Leia and headed to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], R2 and the precious plans he carried were with them.

Having arrived on Yavin 4, the Death Star plans were studied by General [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] and other Rebel officers in the hope of finding an exploitable weakness. In addition, because of the Death Star's unexpected arrival shortly thereafter thanks to a tracking droid smuggled on the ''Falcon'', the personnel also rushed through trying to strategise on how to destroy the Death Star via the plans. They found it in the form of a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] which, if hit directly by a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]], would trigger a chain reaction destroying the battle station. This is precisely what Luke Skywalker did in the proceeding [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

===The Hutt threat===
Following the fall of the Empire, the Death Star Plans were kept by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] in a secure computer system on Coruscant. However, in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], a team of [[Taurill/Legends|Taurill]] [[Commando/Legends|commandos]] broke in during a diplomatic reception for [[Durga Besadii Tai|Durga the Hutt]] and stole a copy of the plans. They delivered them to Durga, who had Bevel Lemelisk use the captured designs to create a new version of the Death Star, the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|''Darksaber'']]. However, this threat was thwarted when the station was [[Battle for the Darksaber|destroyed]] in the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]].<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|&hellip;if you had to throw a dinner party and invite everyone who had ever stolen the Death Star plans, you'd be surprised at how many place settings you'd have to worry about.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/f20080104/indexp2.html|text=Checklist: 10 ''Star Wars'' Superweapons - The Death Star}}</ref>}}
In the early production of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|the original movie]], the hollow dish of the Death Star was designed to be on the equator, but then it was moved to the "northern" hemisphere. However, the old design can still be seen in the grid plan animations in the movie. This is because the animation was created before the prop designers decided to make the change. The original plans displayed in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], set twenty-two years earlier, show the final form.

The grid plan animations shown during the Rebel briefing for the attack on the Death Star late in ''A New Hope'' were an actual computer graphics simulation from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) made by Larry Cuba and Gary Imhoff as part of a project for school at CalArts, and had been included during filming for ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'' (then known as just ''Star Wars''). Originally, the writers and staff planned to thank JPL for assisting in the graphics, but it was changed to the specific programmers' names after one of the programmers, Mike Plesset, pointed out that JPL didn't even know their computers had been used.<ref name="The Death Star Plans ARE in the Main Computer&hellip;and a Special Postcard">{{SW|url=news/death-star-plans-are-in-the-main-computer-and-special-postcard|text=The Death Star Plans ARE in the Main Computer&hellip;and a Special Postcard|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[File:Death_Star_plans_Kenner.jpg|250px|thumb|Kenner's physical "Death Star Plans" card]]
The [[Star Wars (radio)|''A New Hope'' audio drama]] in 1981 is the first to mention rebels on Toprawa transmitting the information to Leia aboard the Tantive IV.<ref name="SW Radio">[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]]</ref> In 1994, the second edition of [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded|''A Guide to the Star Wars Universe'']] would add the character of Bevel Lemelisk as well as the planet Despayre to the plans.<ref name="Guide to SW 2nd">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> The release of [[Star Wars: Dark Forces|''Dark Forces'']] in 1995 saw Kyle Katarn steal the plans from the planet Danuta as part of "[[Operation Skyhook]]."<ref name="DF">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref> In 1998, with the release of ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', the mission in ''Dark Forces'' and the [[Battle of Toprawa]] mentioned in the audio drama and the novel ''[[Rebel Dawn]]'' would be tied together as part of the operation mentioned in ''Dark Forces'' with the information Katarn collected being sent to the rebel cell on Toprawa.<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

In the succeeding years a number of other games would also involve the theft of part of the Death Star Plans. The 1993 [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']] game for PC also had a mission involving the theft of the Death Star Plans however that mission does not get mentioned in other sources leaving its canonicity in question. Other parts of the game are referenced in later media such as the ''Star Wars Encyclopedia'' (1998) but aside from his role as a Y-wing pilot at the Battle of Yavin the theft of the Death Star Plans are not mentioned.<ref name="SWE" /> The 2007 [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']] novel also tied the 2005 video game ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' Death Star mission to the operation as well as giving a reason for the data to be moved to another planet.<ref name="DS" /> While the plans are stolen in ''Battlefront II'' (2005) and [[Star Wars: Lethal Alliance|''Lethal Alliance'']] (2008), it was not the player character's mission to retrieve the plans and the plans do not get transmitted to the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II" /><ref name="Lethal Alliance">''[[Star Wars: Lethal Alliance]]''</ref> A mission reminiscent of the ''X-Wing'' game also appeared in the game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''; however, the game contains a number of missions that do not line up with other parts of canon or would have been impossible outside of the games setting.<ref name="EaW" />

The ''Star Wars'' [[Databank (original)|original Databank]] article on the Death Star acknowledged the contributions of Kyle Katarn, Keyan Farlander, "Rebel spies in the Toprawa system," and other unnamed heroes. The Death Star Uprising and 501st Legion were both mentioned, but the article made no reference to the plans even being involved in this jailbreak.<ref name="databank">{{DB|location|deathstar|Death Star}}</ref>

[[Kenner Products|Kenner's]] 12-inch R2-D2 "large size action figure" released in [[1979]] included a plastic card with graphic stickers on it representing the Death Star plans. An opening panel allowed the card to be held in a compartment in the back of the action figure.<ref name="Kenner Plans">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars (Kenner toy line)|packtype=Large Size Action Figure|pack=Artoo-Detoo (R2-D2)|altlink=https://happybeeps.net/starwars-merchandises/r2-d2-4198}}</ref>
